integration_questions: With mass 0.5 kg, does steering_oscillation on the oval stay near 0.3, or does the lighter robot jitter more?
Does slalom progress move past the 0.17 to 0.18 plateau? If not, the stall is probably controller reaction time rather than inertia.
Does s-bend progress hold at or above 0.6? If it drops, the 0.6 kg value was better and the mass lever is exhausted.
Do wheel slip or line_loss_events rise at bend entries with the lighter mass?

intent: Test whether lower total mass (0.6 to 0.5 kg) lifts the slalom plateau and the s-bend progress on top of the iteration 8 radius and track gains. Only mass changes relative to iteration 8, which scored 417.9 as the best design so far. Expected result: slalom progress above 0.2, s-bend progress at or above 0.6, oval still at 18 or more of 20 finishes, and a score above 417.9.
learning: Iterations 4 to 8 show that sensor footprint 0.012 m, lookahead y=0.08 m and a radius-to-track ratio near 0.4 are the working region. Radius 0.04 m with track 0.10 m lifted s-bend progress strongly but cost some oval stability. The slalom plateau has not moved under any sensing or turn-rate change, so this iteration tests inertia directly. If mass helps, the next step is body_length reduction to cut yaw inertia further.
rationale: Eight races are now on record. Iteration 8 is the best so far (417.9). It raised wheel_radius from 0.035 to 0.040 m and widened wheel_track to 0.10 m, which kept the radius-to-track ratio near the value that worked before. The s-bend progress rose from 0.486 to 0.655, which was the main source of the gain. The oval fell slightly from 20/20 to 19/20 finishes, with steering_oscillation rising from about 0.21 to 0.31. The slalom did not move: progress has sat at 0.16 to 0.18 in every design tested, whatever the track width, row position, footprint or radius. Sensing (footprint 0.008 and 0.016 m, span widening) and turn authority have both been tested, so the remaining untested lever on that plateau is the inertia the robot must overcome in a turn. Yaw inertia is mass*(L^2+W^2)/12, and mass also sets acceleration through the drivetrain. I therefore make one change relative to iteration 8: mass from 0.6 to 0.5 kg, the lowest step that is clearly lighter. Everything else stays at the iteration 8 values, so the effect is isolated. I expect faster response on the slalom and s-bend, which should lift slalom progress above 0.2 and keep s-bend near or above 0.65. The main risk is that lighter mass reduces wheel grip (slip) or makes the oval jitter more, so the Integrator should check steering_oscillation, line_loss_events and oval finishes first. If the oval drops below about 18/20 or oscillation exceeds 0.35, the next step is to return to 0.6 kg and treat the slalom as a controller-side limit.
